newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money climbs amid tighter conditions.
newsitem.headline: German call money climbs amid tighter conditions.

text.p: German call money rates began the week on a firmer note as liquidity conditions tightened amid continuing shifts of funds and slightly lower reserve holdings.
Dealers said the bulk of trades was conducted around 3.16 percent with trades ranging from 3.12 to 3.20 percent compared with Friday's bulk of trades at 3.10 percent.

Some tightness can be attributed to relatively low reserve holdings at the Bundesbank, dealers said, adding however that it was too early to predict how the Bundesbank might tackle these conditions at the weekly tender award on Wednesday.
Dealers also said that some tightness might be caused by the federal government which appears to be holding off in re-investing some funds.
"It it not as though there is not enough money in the system, but the government might not be re-investing it right away," a trader said.

Consequently dealers said it would be difficult to make any serious predictions about whether the Bundesbank might add funds at this week's tender award, when a repo pact for 77 billion marks expires.
Daily holdings in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank stood at 37.7 billion marks on Friday compared with 37.5 billion marks a day earlier.
Average holdings for the month however slipped to 40.5 billion marks on Sunday from 41.9 billion marks, the Bundesbank said.
Lombard borrowings stood at 100 million marks on Friday after they were negligible on Thursday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.18700 percent on Monday after 3.13700 percent on Friday.
